data.note: While Raging, immediately after taking the Attack action on your turn you can make one additional melee weapon attack as a bonus action (Frenzied Strike). On a hit, you can choose to push the target up to 10 ft or knock it prone. Frenzy no longer imposes exhaustion in the 2024 rules. Push/prone rider requires manual tracking; engine cannot enforce 'after Attack action' timing.

activities.name: Frenzied Strike
activities.note: Requires Rage. Use immediately after your Attack action. On hit: push target 10 ft or knock Prone (manual tracking).

data.note: While Raging you can't be Charmed or Frightened. If Charmed or Frightened when you enter rage, the effect is suspended for the rage's duration.

As an action, you can frighten someone with your menace. Choose one creature that you can see within 30 feet of you. If the creature can see or hear you, it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier) or be Frightened of you until the end of your next turn. On subsequent turns you can take an action to extend the duration of this effect on the frightened creature until the end of your next turn; this effect ends if the creature ends its turn out of line of sight or more than 60 feet away from you. If the creature succeeds on its saving throw, you can't use this feature on that creature again for 24 hours. v0 surfaces as an action save activity; duration extension and 24-hour lockout are tracked by the DM.
When you take damage from a creature that is within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to make one melee weapon attack against that creature.
Gain proficiency in any 3 skills of your choice. Engine emits proficiency.skill.<slug> modifiers from choices.skillProficiencies array picks.

When a creature you can see within 60 feet that can hear you makes an attack roll, an ability check, or a damage roll, you can use your reaction to expend a use of Bardic Inspiration and subtract the rolled die from the creature's roll. Can be used after seeing the roll but before the DM declares whether it succeeds. v0 surfaces as a trigger; Bardic Inspiration die accounting lives on the bard class row.

Learn two spells from any class's spell list (must be castable level or cantrip). Engine injects chosen spells as deferred active-content refs via choices.spell. Player stores picks in featureChoices[slug].spell.spells.

When you make an ability check, you can expend one use of Bardic Inspiration. Roll a Bardic Inspiration die and add the number rolled to your ability check. You can choose to do so after you roll the die for the ability check but before the DM tells you whether you succeed or fail. v0 surfaces as a tagged trigger on self ability checks; Bardic Inspiration die accounting lives on the bard class row.

Always-prepared Domain spells. SRD pack coverage: Bless, Cure Wounds, Spiritual Weapon, Mass Healing Word injected via spellListAdditions. Missing from SRD pack: Lesser Restoration, Revivify, Aura of Life, Death Ward, Mass Cure Wounds, Raise Dead.

Whenever you cast a spell of level 1+ that restores HP to a creature, the creature regains an additional 2 + the spell's level HP. v0 surfaces as a tagged action-modifier on heal-typed activities; the additive amount isn't applied to the heal roll yet.

Use one Channel Divinity charge as an action to create a pool of healing equal to 5 × your cleric level. Distribute the pool among creatures within 30 ft you can see (including yourself); each creature can only be brought up to half its HP max with this pool. The pool total is 5×clericLevel — 'fiveTimesClericLevel' is not in the supported magic identifier list, so v0 tags this as a trait and notes the formula for the DM/player to apply. Consumes a Channel Divinity use from the cleric class row.

activities.name: Preserve Life (Channel Divinity)
activities.note: Healing pool = 5 × cleric level. Distribute among visible creatures within 30 ft; each creature may only recover up to half its HP maximum from this pool.

data.note: When you cast a spell of level 1+ that restores HP to a creature other than yourself, you also regain HP equal to 2 + the spell's level. v0 surfaces as a tagged action-modifier on heal-typed activities targeting others; the self-heal credit isn't applied automatically — 'self.heal-on-heal-other' is not in the evaluator.

When you would normally roll one or more dice to restore hit points with a spell, you instead use the highest number possible for each die. For example, instead of restoring 2d6 hit points to a creature, you restore 12. v0 surfaces as a tagged action-modifier on heal-typed spell casts; the dice-maximization isn't applied automatically — 'damage.die.min' (maximize dice) is not in the evaluator.

You always have the following Druid spells always-prepared (selected from your chosen land's spell list — Arctic, Coast, Desert, Forest, Grassland, Mountain, Swamp, or Underdark). Choose your land at L3; spells don't count against your prepared limit. v0 surfaces this as a flag + a choice; auto-prep injection isn't wired.

Magic action, expend Wild Shape use. CON save (Spell DC). Failure: 2d6 necrotic (half on success). Also heal selected creatures 2d6. Scales by druid level: L10→3d6, L14→4d6, L17→5d6. Dice expressed via perClass druid table.

Once per long rest, when you finish a short rest you can recover expended spell slots whose combined level is no greater than half your druid level (rounded up), with no individual slot above level 5. v0 surfaces a 1/long-rest utility; the slot-recovery accounting is left to the player.
You are immune to the Poisoned condition and to disease. You also have Resistance to poison damage.

When a Beast or Plant creature attacks you, it must make a Wisdom saving throw against your Spell Save DC. On a failed save, the creature must choose a different target or lose the attack or spell. On a success, the creature is immune to this feature for 24 hours. v0 surfaces as a tagged trait; the save-redirect mechanic is not expressible in the current evaluator.
Your weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20 on the d20. In 2024 this applies to weapon attacks (spell attacks do not benefit).

When you roll Initiative, add your Strength modifier to the roll. You also have a Climb Speed and Swim Speed equal to your Speed (dynamically equals walkSpeed via evaluateValue). When you make a running long jump, add your STR modifier to the distance — jump math is not modelled in v0.
You can choose a second option from the Fighting Style class feature. v0 surfaces the choice; picks live on character.classes[].choices.additionalFightingStyle.
Your weapon attacks now score a critical hit on a roll of 18–20. This supersedes Improved Critical (19-20) gained at L3.

When you hit a creature with one of the attacks granted by your Flurry of Blows, you can impose one of the following effects on that target: (a) it must make a DEX save (DC = your Ki/Focus Save DC) or be knocked prone; (b) it must make a STR save or be pushed up to 15 ft from you; (c) it can't take reactions until the end of your next turn (no save). v0 surfaces as a tagged action-modifier on Flurry of Blows attacks; effect selection and save resolution are left to play.

As a bonus action, expend 3 Focus Points to heal yourself for 2d8 + your WIS modifier HP. Heal amount and dice are correct; focus-point deduction (3 per use) is player-managed since the engine has no per-ability-cost deduction from a shared pool.

activities.name: Wholeness of Body
activities.note: Costs 3 Focus Points per use — player must deduct from their focus pool manually.

data.note: At the end of a long rest you gain the effect of a Sanctuary spell (Wis save DC = your Focus Save DC) that lasts until the start of your next long rest or until you attack a creature, force a creature to make a saving throw, or cast a spell. v0 surfaces as a tagged trait; auto-application of Sanctuary on rest isn't wired.

When you hit a creature with an unarmed strike, you can spend 4 Focus Points to start imperceptible vibrations in the target's body. The vibrations last for a number of days equal to your monk level. The vibrations are harmless unless you use your action to end them — at that point the target must make a CON saving throw (Focus Save DC). On a failed save the target drops to 0 HP. On a success the target takes 10d10 necrotic damage. You can have only one creature under this effect at a time. v0 surfaces as a tagged utility activity; CON save resolution is handled by the DM.

activities.name: Quivering Palm (Activate)
activities.note: Spend 4 Focus Points. Triggers on a successful unarmed strike hit. The vibrations last for a number of days equal to your monk level.

activities.name: Quivering Palm (Release)
activities.note: On failed save: target drops to 0 HP. On successful save: 10d10 necrotic damage. Requires target to be under active Quivering Palm vibrations.

data.note: You always have the following always-prepared paladin spells: L3 Protection from Evil and Good, Shield of Faith; L5 Lesser Restoration, Zone of Truth; L9 Beacon of Hope, Dispel Magic; L13 Freedom of Movement, Guardian of Faith; L17 Commune, Flame Strike. They don't count against your prepared limit. v0 surfaces this as a flag; auto-prep injection isn't wired.

As a Bonus Action, expend a use of Channel Divinity to imbue one weapon you're holding with positive energy for 1 minute. For the duration, attacks with the weapon gain a bonus to attack rolls equal to your CHA modifier (minimum +1), and the weapon emits bright light in a 20-ft radius and dim light 20 ft beyond that. The attack bonus applies to attack rolls only — Sacred Weapon does not grant extra damage. Consumes a Channel Divinity use from the paladin class row.

When a creature within 60 ft hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction and expend a use of Channel Divinity to deal radiant damage to the attacker equal to 2d8 + your Paladin level. The attacker can make a CON saving throw (your Spell Save DC) for half damage. Consumes a Channel Divinity use from the paladin class row.

You and allies within 10 ft are immune to Charmed (expanded to 30 ft at L18 via class Aura Expansion). Aura suppressed while Incapacitated — engine cannot gate outboundEffects on !condition, so that edge case requires manual handling.

You can call on the spirits of nature to reveal certain strengths and weaknesses of a creature you can see within 120 ft as a bonus action. The DM tells you if the creature has any Damage Immunities, Resistances, or Vulnerabilities. v0 surfaces a bonus-action utility; the information reveal is a DM-side action.
Choose one option (Colossus Slayer, Horde Breaker, or Giant Killer). Engine loads the chosen sub-feature via choices.feature; player stores pick in featureChoices[hunters-prey].
Once per turn when you hit a creature with a weapon and the target is below its HP maximum, deal an extra 1d8 damage of the weapon's type.

Once per turn when you hit a creature with a weapon and the target is below its HP maximum, deal an extra 1d8 damage of the weapon's type. Engine cannot check target HP — player enables toggle only when applicable. Fixed: weapon.classification (invalid, now attack.classification) and damage.bonus string (now damage.dice).
Once per turn when you make a weapon attack, make another weapon attack against a different creature within 5 ft of the original target and within your weapon's range.
When a Large or larger creature within 5 ft hits or misses you with an attack, use your reaction to make one melee weapon attack against that creature.

Choose one of the following at L7 (pick lives on character.classes[].choices.defensiveTactics):
• Escape the Horde: Opportunity attacks against you are made with Disadvantage.
• Multiattack Defense: When a creature hits you with an attack, you gain +4 to AC against all subsequent attacks made by that creature for the rest of the turn.
• Steel Will: You have Advantage on saving throws against the Frightened condition.
v0 implements Escape the Horde and Steel Will as stat-modifiers; Multiattack Defense is a trigger-based effect that can't be fully expressed in the evaluator.

modifiers.note: Opportunity attacks against you are made with Disadvantage. Not a supported target in the evaluator — surfaced as a tag.
Multiattack Defense: +4 AC vs. subsequent attacks from the same attacker this turn. Not expressible in the evaluator — surfaced as a tag.

data.note:
Choose one of the following at L11 (pick lives on character.classes[].choices.hunterMultiattack):
• Volley: As an action, make ranged attacks against any number of creatures within 10 ft of a point you can see within your ranged weapon's range. You make a separate attack roll for each target, using the same ammunition or thrown weapon for all attacks.
• Whirlwind Attack: As an action, make melee attacks against any number of creatures within 5 ft of you, with a separate attack roll for each target.
v0 surfaces both as action attack activities; target selection is left to play.

activities.name: Volley
activities.note: Ranged attack against any number of targets within 10 ft of a chosen point within your ranged weapon's range. Separate attack roll per target.

activities.name: Whirlwind Attack
activities.note: Melee attack against any number of targets within 5 ft. Separate attack roll per target.

data.note:
Choose one of the following at L15 (pick lives on character.classes[].choices.superiorHuntersDefense):
• Evasion: When you are subjected to an effect that allows a DEX saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage on a success and only half on a failure.
• Stand Against the Tide: When a hostile creature misses you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction to force the creature to repeat the attack against another creature of your choice (other than itself) within the attacker's reach.
• Uncanny Dodge: When an attacker you can see hits you with an attack roll, use your reaction to halve the damage (already on rogue at L5 — this provides it to rangers at L15).
v0 surfaces Evasion as a tag (evaluator can't express the full DEX save flip); Stand Against the Tide as a trigger tag; Uncanny Dodge as a tag.

modifiers.note: Evasion: no damage on successful DEX save, half on failure. Not expressible in the evaluator — surfaced as a tag.
Stand Against the Tide: redirect missed attack to another creature within attacker's reach. Not expressible in the evaluator.
Uncanny Dodge: halve damage from a seen attacker as a reaction. Not expressible in the evaluator.

data.note: You can use the bonus action granted by Cunning Action to take the Utilize action, to make a Sleight of Hand check, or to use Thieves' Tools to disarm a trap or pick a lock. v0 surfaces this as a tagged trait — the underlying bonus-action grant is on the rogue Cunning Action feature row.

You gain a Climb Speed equal to your Speed (dynamically equals walkSpeed via evaluateValue). When you make a running jump, your jump distance increases by your DEX modifier — jump math is not modelled in v0.

You can take the Hide action as a bonus action. Additionally, you have Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks if you move no more than half your Speed on the same turn. v0 surfaces the Hide bonus action as an activity; the conditional Stealth Advantage is tagged.

modifiers.note: Advantage on Stealth checks when moving no more than half Speed this turn. Conditional advantage isn't expressible in the evaluator — surfaced as a tag.

data.note: You have learned enough about the workings of magic that you can improvise the use of items even when they are not intended for you. You can use any spell scroll, provided the spell is on the Wizard spell list. When you use a scroll this way, treat the spell as if cast using the scroll's spell level; if it isn't a spell you could normally cast, the relevant spellcasting ability for it is Intelligence. Additionally, you can use any other magic item that requires attunement to a class, race, or other group you don't belong to. v0 surfaces as a tagged trait.

You have become adept at laying ambushes and quickly escaping danger. You can take two turns during the first round of any combat. You take your first turn at your normal initiative and your second turn at your initiative minus 10. You can't use this feature when you are Surprised.

modifiers.note: Two turns in the first round of combat (first at normal initiative, second at initiative − 10). Multi-turn initiative logic isn't expressible in the evaluator — surfaced as a tag.

data.note: Your hit point maximum increases by an amount equal to your Sorcerer level. When you aren't wearing armor, your AC = 13 + your DEX modifier.

Choose a dragon type at L3 (black: acid; blue: lightning; brass: fire; bronze: lightning; copper: acid; gold: fire; green: poison; red: fire; silver: cold; white: cold). You gain the ability to speak, read, and write Draconic. The chosen dragon's damage type governs Elemental Affinity (L6) and Dragon Wings (L14). Pick lives on character.classes[].choices.dragonAncestry.

When you cast a spell that deals damage of the type associated with your Draconic Ancestry, you can add your CHA modifier to one damage roll of that spell. You also gain Resistance to that damage type. The dynamic resistance (based on chosen ancestry) and the ancestry-type predicate can't be expressed in the evaluator without per-character data — v0 surfaces a conditional action-modifier flag and a trait tag; full resistance must be wired at character-build time.

Toggle is off by default — player enables it when casting a spell of their ancestry's damage type. The ancestry-type predicate (damage.type.matches-dragon-ancestry) was removed as it has no evaluator support; player management is the correct v0 pattern. The CHA-mod damage bonus resolves correctly via evaluateValue(chaMod). Resistance must be wired separately at character-build time (trait.elemental-affinity-resistance is a flag; actual resistance added via the draconic-ancestry sub-feature).
You sprout draconic wings and gain a Fly Speed equal to your Speed (not while wearing heavy armor). Fly speed dynamically equals walkSpeed via UPGRADE mode.

As a Bonus Action, you can spend 5 Sorcery Points to draw on this power and exude an aura of awe or fear (your choice) to a distance of 60 feet. For 1 minute or until you lose Concentration, each hostile creature that starts its turn in this aura must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (Spell Save DC) or be Charmed (awe) or Frightened (fear) of you until the aura ends. v0 surfaces as a concentration bonus-action save activity with 5 sorcery point cost; tracking sorcery point deduction is left to the player.

activities.name: Draconic Presence
activities.note: Costs 5 Sorcery Points. Each hostile creature that starts its turn in the aura must save. Choice of Charmed (awe) or Frightened (fear) aura is made when activated.

data.note: Always-prepared Patron spells. SRD pack coverage: Burning Hands, Scorching Ray, Fireball, Wall of Fire injected via spellListAdditions. Missing from SRD pack: Command, Blindness/Deafness, Stinking Cloud, Fire Shield.

When you reduce a creature to 0 HP, or a creature within 30 ft of you is reduced to 0 HP, you gain Temporary HP equal to your Warlock level + CHA modifier (minimum 1). Amount expressed as { sum: [warlockLevel, chaMod] } using the evaluateValue sum shape.

When you make an ability check or saving throw, you can add 1d10 to the roll. You can do so after seeing the roll but before any of its effects occur. Once used, you can't use this feature again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

Choose one damage type when you finish a Short or Long Rest. You gain Resistance to that damage type until you choose a different type with this feature. Resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing from non-magical attacks doesn't count. v0 surfaces as a choice/utility activity; the dynamic resistance choice is tagged and must be updated per rest. The engine should apply resistance.<type> dynamically from the player's choice.

activities.name: Fiendish Resilience (Choose Resistance)
activities.note: Choose a damage type to gain Resistance to for the next rest period.

data.note: When you hit a creature with an attack roll, you can hurl it momentarily to the lower planes. The creature disappears, screams in agony, and is teleported back at the end of your next turn. It takes 8d10 psychic damage when it returns. If it is not a Fiend, it is Frightened of you for 1 minute on a successful return (WIS save to end each turn). Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest. v0 surfaces as a 1/long-rest utility triggered on a hit; the damage and Frightened application are modelled as a follow-up save activity.

activities.name: Hurl Through Hell (on hit)
activities.note: Triggers on a successful attack hit. Target disappears until end of your next turn, then takes 8d10 psychic damage and may become Frightened.

activities.name: Hurl Through Hell (Return Damage)
activities.note: 8d10 psychic damage on return. Non-Fiends: WIS save or Frightened for 1 minute. WIS save at end of each turn to end Frightened.

data.note: When you adopt this subclass at L3, you gain two free Evocation spells of your choice from the Wizard spell list, added to your spellbook. Whenever you gain a Wizard level after L3, you can add one Evocation spell to your spellbook for free (no gold cost). v0 surfaces the L3 picks as a choice; ongoing per-level bonus picks aren't tracked.

When you cast an Evocation spell that affects other creatures you can see, you can choose a number of those creatures equal to 1 + the spell's level. The chosen creatures automatically succeed on their saving throws against the spell, and they take no damage if they would normally take half damage on a success. v0 surfaces a tagged action-modifier on Evocation casts; ally-protection logic is left to play.

When a creature succeeds on a saving throw against your cantrip, the creature takes half the cantrip's damage (if any) but suffers no additional effect from the cantrip. v0 surfaces a tagged action-modifier on cantrip cast activities; half-on-save semantics are left to the engine.
Whenever you cast an Evocation spell from the Wizard spell list, you can add your Intelligence modifier to one damage roll of that spell.

When you cast a Wizard spell of level 1–5 that deals damage, you can deal maximum damage with that spell — even if it normally allows a saving throw for half damage. The first time you do so, you suffer no ill effect. If you use this feature again before finishing a Long Rest, you take 2d12 necrotic damage per level of the spell, immediately after casting it. Each additional use before a long rest adds another 2d12 necrotic per spell level (so second time: 2d12×level, third time: 4d12×level, etc.). v0 surfaces as a tagged action-modifier on Wizard evocation casts of level 1–5; the self-damage escalation is tracked by the player.
